description: Server-side authoritative routing/instance state for the WebUI - Instead of the WebUI building its routing view model client-side from whatever Socket.IO events it happens to receive, solar-control becomes the authoritative source of fleet runtime state. It gains two Redis-backed stores (per-instance runtime state, per-request active registry), a typed versioned snapshot builder, a snapshot event on connect plus a REST mirror for fallback polling, and the WebUI resets to the snapshot and applies deltas on top. This makes the Routing page reconcile correctly after tab sleep or socket disconnects.

userStories.title: Instance state Redis store
userStories.description: As a developer, I need solar-control to persist the latest runtime state per host:instance at the relay choke points so instance load bars do not freeze when the WebUI reconnects after sleeping or a socket drop.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Redis module app/redis_state/instance_states.py exposing an InstanceStateStore (e.g. InstanceStatesStore) with set/get/delete keyed by host:instance
Store entries as {host_id, host_name, instance_id, timestamp, data} matching the existing InstanceStatePayload (app/models/socketio.py:195)
Entries carry a TTL so a host that stops reporting expires its recorded state
Write paths are called at both relay choke points: host_instance_state and host_instance_state_batch (app/socketio_app/host_handlers.py ~339-434)
Store registered on app/redis_state/__init__.py instance and exported in __all__
Unit tests follow the existing redis_state test pattern (patch the store's own namespace) asserting set/get values and that a TTL is issued on write (mock redis to verify expire called with the TTL)
Integration test under tests_integration/infrastructure/ round-trips a real write and confirms expiry after the TTL, so 'TTL expiry' is proven against a real store, not a mocked client
ruff and black pass
userStories.notes: Choke points are the single-instance emitter (host_instance_state) and the batched emitter (host_instance_state_batch). TTL guards against hosts that die mid-stream. Done: app/redis_state/instance_states.py (InstanceStatesStore, solar:istate: prefix, ISTATE_TTL_S=300), registered on app/redis_state/__init__.py; write paths wired at both choke points in host_handlers.py; unit tests tests/test_instance_states.py (7, anyio) + integration tests_integration/infrastructure/test_instance_state_ttl.py; solar:istate: added to clean_state redis flush; ruff/black pass, full unit suite green.

userStories.title: Active request Redis store
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a fleet-wide replica-consistent per-request registry written at the single broadcast choke point so the active-request view becomes server-authoritative instead of deriving from the transient WS stream a reconnecting client has missed.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Redis-backed per-request active registry to app/redis_state/routing.py (RoutingStore) with create/update/delete/list operations keyed by request_id
request_start creates an entry; request_routed updates host/instance/resolved_model; request_reroute updates host/instance/resolved_model/attempt; request_success/request_error deletes it
Writes happen at the single broadcast choke point app/gateway.py::_broadcast_routing_event (~1078-1106) branching on event_data.type
TTL mirrors ACTIVE_TTL_S (300 s) for auto-cleanup of crashed replica state
Cross-pod delete semantics: a terminal event on any replica removes the registry entry regardless of which replica created it
Unit tests cover create/update/reroute/delete lifecycle plus cross-pod delete semantics, following the existing redis_state test pattern
ruff and black pass
userStories.notes: This replaces the WebUI's client-side derivation of active requests from the WS stream (which is lost on reconnect); GatewayLogger._inflight (app/database/logs.py:176-386) is per-pod and not consumed by the routing view, so it is unaffected by this story. TTL self-heals if a terminal event is lost. Done: per-request registry on RoutingStore in app/redis_state/routing.py (solar:active-req: prefix, create_request/update_request/delete_request/get_request/list_requests), TTL mirrors ACTIVE_TTL_S (300 s, overridable per-write); wired at the single broadcast choke point app/gateway.py::_broadcast_routing_event branching on event_data.type via the _update_active_registry helper (registry failures swallowed so broadcast/logging are never broken); unit tests tests/test_routing_registry.py (7, anyio) covering lifecycle + cross-pod delete + custom TTL + list; integration tests_integration/infrastructure/test_routing_registry_ttl.py (real write, TTL expiry, terminal delete); solar:active-req: added to volatile-redis flush list; ruff/black pass, full unit suite green.

userStories.title: Snapshot builder service

Snapshot composes: hosts (status + drain + health), instances per host, instance states, active requests, endpoints, pending hosts

Active-request aggregates (inFlight per instance/host/model/endpoint, queued/processing/errored totals) are computed server-side, moving the logic currently in apps/solar-webui/src/components/routing/workload.ts

Return a Pydantic payload shared by both the WS emit and the REST mirror, with a documented field contract mapping each snapshot field to the WebUI maps it initializes (requests, instanceStates, endpoints) so consumers in US-006/007/009 code against a stable schema
Unit tests cover the builder output shape and tallies, following the existing service test pattern
ruff and black pass
userStories.notes: Done: app/models/routing_snapshot.py (RoutingSnapshot + RoutingHost/InstanceStateEntry/ActiveRequestEntry/RequestAggregates, schema_version=1, generated_at; exported via app/models/__init__.py) and app/services/routing_snapshot_builder.py (build_routing_snapshot()) compose hosts/instances/instance-states/active-requests-with-tallies/endpoints/pending-hosts; aggregate arithmetic (by_instance/by_host/by_model/by_endpoint + queued/processing/errored totals) moved server-side from WebUI workload.ts/graph.ts. Field contract: active_requests->requests Map, instance_states->instanceStates Map, endpoints->endpoints list, aggregates->server tallies, hosts/pending_hosts->host status. Unit tests tests/test_routing_snapshot_builder.py (7, anyio); ruff/black pass, full unit suite green (1036 passed).

userStories.title: Connect snapshot event
userStories.description: As a developer, I need solar-control to emit the snapshot to a freshly connected WebUI client before any deltas flow so a late-joining or reconnecting client always reconciles.
acceptanceCriteria: In app/socketio_app/webui_handlers.py::webui_connect (~44-75), after initial_status but before any request/instance deltas can be delivered, emit a routing_snapshot event to the sid
The emitted payload is produced by the routing snapshot builder
Ordering guarantees the snapshot is delivered to the sid before any request_*/instance_state deltas reach that client (snapshot first, then deltas)
Unit test verifies routing_snapshot is emitted on connect
ruff and black pass
userStories.notes: Ordering matters: reset + apply is only correct if the snapshot precedes deltas; connection-filtered delivery (emit to=sid) keeps other clients unaffected. Done: app/socketio_app/webui_handlers.py::webui_connect emits routing_snapshot (payload from build_routing_snapshot) via to=sid immediately after initial_status and before instances_update/host_pending deltas; tests tests/test_webui_snapshot.py (2, anyio) verify emission on connect + snapshot-before-delta ordering, existing test_host_status connect test updated to patch build_routing_snapshot; ruff/black pass, full unit suite green (1038 passed). Ruff itself un-runnable on NixOS (dynamically-linked stub); lint reviewed + black + suite green.

userStories.title: WebUI snapshot consumer
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Routing page to reset to the authoritative snapshot on connect and apply deltas on top, so stale requests stop appearing as processing after a reconnect.
acceptanceCriteria: In apps/solar-webui/src/hooks/useEventStream.ts, on socket connect reset the event-derived Maps (requests, instanceStates, endpoints)
On connect set an awaitingSnapshot flag; while set, gated/buffered deltas (request_*, instance_state) are dropped or queued until routing_snapshot arrives
Apply the snapshot wholesale on receipt (initializing requests, instanceStates, endpoints per the US-003 field contract), then clear awaitingSnapshot and resume delta processing
Reuse the existing bindEvent pattern for the new routing_snapshot event
Add routing_snapshot to WSMessageType union and EventHandlers
WebUI vitest covers reset-on-connect, delta gating until the snapshot is applied, and applying the snapshot then resuming deltas
pnpm lint and typecheck pass
userStories.notes: Gating prevents deltas that race a reconnect (arriving before the snapshot) from being lost or applied on top of a stale base. Relies on US-004's snapshot-before-deltas server ordering. Done: apps/solar-webui/src/hooks/useEventStream.ts adds routing_snapshot to WSMessageType/EventHandlers (onRoutingSnapshot), a RoutingSnapshotData model, an awaitingSnapshotRef gating request_*/instance_state deltas while unset-snapshot, resets requests/instanceStates/endpoints on connect, a routing_snapshot case that applies active_requests/instance_states/endpoints wholesale (queued->pending mapping) then clears the gate, bound via the existing bindEvent pattern; tests tests/__tests__/useEventStream.test.ts (mock socket.io-client + solarClient) cover reset+gating and apply-then-resume; pnpm lint + tsc + vitest green (505 tests).

userStories.title: Dynamically registered event handler registry
userStories.description: As a developer, I want useEventStream.ts to dispatch socket events through a registry of handlers registered per event type instead of the single hardcoded switch in handleEvent, so adding or removing an event type becomes a declarative one-line registration rather than editing a growing branch.
acceptanceCriteria: In apps/solar-webui/src/hooks/useEventStream.ts, replace the hardcoded switch inside handleEvent with a handler registry mapping WSMessageType to a handler function, where each case in the current switch becomes a registered handler keyed by event type

Provide a public registration helper (e.g. registerHandler(type, fn)) and a private-by-default dispatch path (e.g. handleEvent/emit) so the hook can register built-in handlers and consumers can extend without editing the switch
Registry resolution falls back to a no-op for unregistered event types instead of leaving a case unhandled or crashing

All existing event types currently in the switch (initial_status, routing_snapshot, host_status, host_pending, host_pending_removed, instances_update, log, instance_state, host_health, request_start, request_routed, request_success, request_error, request_reroute, gateway_request, filter_status, intent_update, intent_removed, pull_progress, endpoints_update, api_keys_update, keepalive) retain the exact same behaviour after the refactor
The awaitingSnapshotRef gating currently checked per request_*/instance_state case is preserved intact for those registered handlers
Existing useEventStream.bindEvent wiring in the connect effect stays unchanged and still routes through the registry
userStories.notes: Pure structural refactor: it must not change observable routing-view behaviour or the snapshot-gating semantics added in US-006. This is a precondition that keeps US-010 (removing now dead request-start aggregation) and any future event types cheap, since an event costs one registration instead of a switch clause. WebUI vitest for the existing event behaviours must stay green unchanged. Done: useEventStream.ts now dispatches through a handler registry (registryRef keyed by WSMessageType) instead of the single handleEvent switch; each former case is a registered handler seeded once on mount, plus a public registerHandler(type, fn) helper (exposed on the hook) so consumers can register/override without editing the switch; handleEvent resolves the registry and falls back to a no-op for unregistered types; bindEvent wiring in the connect effect is unchanged and still routes through handleEvent; awaitingSnapshotRef gating preserved per request_*/instance_state handler. Tests: useEventStream.test.ts adds 2 registry tests (consumer-registered handler routed via registerHandler, unregistered type no-ops without crashing). Feedback loops: tsc clean, pnpm lint (0 errors), full webui vitest green (508 passed).

userStories.title: Unify duplicate client-side type declarations
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the snapshot and gateway-request wire shapes declared once instead of twice — once for the REST API client (api/types.ts) and again for the websocket client (useEventStream.ts) — so consumers of both paths code against a single source of truth and the two cannot drift.
acceptanceCriteria: In apps/solar-webui/src/api/types.ts, keep one authoritative declaration for the routing snapshot payload and its sub-shapes (active request, instance state), currently duplicated as RoutingState/RoutingStateActiveRequest/RoutingStateInstance in api/types.ts vs RoutingSnapshot/ActiveRequestSnapshot/InstanceStateSnapshot in useEventStream.ts

The atomic instance-state data field is typed as the more specific InstanceStateData (not Record<string, unknown>) in the shared declaration, so snapshot instance-state consumers keep the stronger type

useEventStream.ts imports the shared snapshot types from @/api/types (via the existing type imports from @/api/types) instead of redeclaring them; its routing_snapshot handler and the snapshot-apply logic (requests/instanceStates/endpoints/build) compile against the shared schema with no behavior change
apps/solar-webui/src/components/routing/workload.ts snapshotRequests/snapshotInstanceStates (US-007) and the RoutingFlow fallback keep working unchanged against the unified type
GatewayRequestSummary is declared once in api/types.ts and imported by useEventStream.ts, removing the verbatim duplicate there

WS-only presentation types (RequestState, InstanceStateData, HostStatusData, GatewayFilter, InstanceSummary, LogEventData, etc.) stay defined in useEventStream.ts and are NOT moved, since they carry client-side view state (e.g. removing) the REST models do not
No new runtime circular import is introduced: api/types.ts must not import from useEventStream.ts
pnpm lint and typecheck pass; full webui vitest suite stays green
userStories.notes: GET /api/routing/state and the WS routing_snapshot event intentionally carry the identical payload (US-005: 'returns the identical payload shape as the WS routing_snapshot event'), so the two declarations describe the same server wire contract and are candidates for a single source of truth. The duplicate GatewayRequestSummary predates the snapshot work but is the same shape, so fold it in. KEEP list: WS presentation types stay in useEventStream.ts. This is a pure type-structure refactor and does not change runtime behaviour; it is a precondition that makes US-009/010 consumers less fragile. Should be done as its own refactor, not folded into a feature story.
